why: A GS1 prefix identifies the Member Organisation that ISSUED the number, not who owns the brand or where the money goes. A Serbian company can and does register numbers through another country's GS1 organisation.

Concrete, verified case that forced this file to exist (owner, 2026-09-12): barcode 3870508000157 is a 40g bag of Chipsy. Its prefix is 387 -- GS1 Bosnia and Herzegovina -- so a prefix-only check calls it 'not Serbian' and clears it. Open Food Facts returns brands = 'Chipsy, Marbo, Pepsico' for that exact barcode: it is Marbo Product, Backa Maglic, Serbia. The revenue is Serbian regardless of which GS1 office issued the number.
So the prefix table is necessary but NOT sufficient. This file is the override: an explicit, evidence-carrying list of brands and barcodes that are boycott targets whatever their prefix says.
DIRECTION OF THE OVERRIDE IS ONE-WAY. This file can only ever ADD a boycott verdict, never remove one. Nothing here can clear an 860-prefixed product.
confidenceRule: Every entry carries a sourceUrl. A brand is listed only where its Serbian ownership is documented, never inferred from a name that sounds Serbian.
